issues.title: Integrate Provably Fast Falcon-512 optimizations into hybrid wallet migration
issues.body:
## Outcome
Reduce the cost of SHAKE-256 Falcon-512 verification in this project's hybrid accounts while preserving ECDSA AND Falcon authorization, existing keys and wallet migration behavior.

Research on 2026-10-26 found that the vendored verifier crates match the challenge baseline bece5c07eeea5784e570c01108ec000d2d04ae40. The live results reported 48.40M baseline verification gas, 24.40M for compact candidate fj_3a0b1c78817845a68e1e907928a541e4, and 24.10M for record fj_c3459a8b07a54bd5828d3fdde899c4e0. These are external benchmark results, not measurements of this project's optimized hybrid account.

## Delivery sequence
1. PF-01: Pin sources and reproduce the baseline and candidates.
2. PF-02: Integrate an isolated optimized hybrid verifier.
3. PF-03 and PF-04: Establish correctness, security evidence, deployability and real transaction savings.
4. PF-05 and PF-06: Make verifier replacement safe and validate wallet migration paths.
5. PF-07: Release a versioned testnet integration and reproducible results.
6. PF-08: Prepare upstream adoption and independent review.
7. PF-09 and PF-10: Track future native Keccak and FN-DSA compatibility separately.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] PF-01 through PF-07 complete with linked evidence.
- [ ] After registration, both ECDSA and Falcon remain mandatory for transaction authorization and privileged changes. Initial migration is authorized by the old wallet and additionally checks the new hybrid key-possession proof; the existing restricted bootstrap exception is not broadened.
- [ ] Browser/Python signing compatibility and existing account key/storage compatibility are demonstrated.
- [ ] Selected verifier fits target-network class, gas, step and libfunc limits with documented margin.
- [ ] Gas claims distinguish bare verification, account validation, full transactions and migration.
- [ ] Release remains explicitly experimental/testnet-only. PF-08 prepares independent review; production use requires the actual review, resolution of relevant findings and a separate release decision.

## Sources
- https://postquantum.provably.fast/scoring
- https://postquantum.provably.fast/api/participation/falcon/results
- https://postquantum.provably.fast/safe

PF-01 through PF-07 define the testnet delivery milestone. PF-08 remains tracked separately until review preparation is complete; completing this milestone is not production approval. PF-09 and PF-10 are deferred research.

issues.title: Pin and reproduce Provably Fast Falcon-512 baseline and candidate results
issues.body:
## Outcome
Establish immutable source provenance and repeatable local measurements before choosing an optimization.

## Scope
- Archive a timestamped result snapshot and stable patch download URLs. Research-time full-record patch SHA-256: 23f3c793b3f9c8b89e787b0492009a36ce4e981cb1ce54eed6defff331b7d2f9; independently verify the downloaded bytes.
- Pin OpenZeppelin baseline bece5c07eeea5784e570c01108ec000d2d04ae40 and verify the vendored source against it.
- Archive exact cumulative patches, SHA-256 digests, result metadata, contributors and MIT notices for:
  - Compact: fj_3a0b1c78817845a68e1e907928a541e4.
  - Record at research time: fj_c3459a8b07a54bd5828d3fdde899c4e0.
- Preserve a pinned choice even if the leaderboard changes. Check later withdrawals/breaks before adoption.
- Pin Scarb 2.18.0, Foundry 0.59.0 and universal-sierra-compiler 2.9.1 for challenge reproduction; document any differences in project/network tooling.
- Reproduce baseline and candidate gas with an independently generated public corpus covering eight- and nine-block SHAKE cases. The private held-out challenge corpus is unavailable; do not claim exact reproduction of its mean.
- Capture generated artifact sizes and commands/environment metadata.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Source/patch hashes, licenses, provenance and reproduction commands are committed.
- [ ] Baseline and both candidates are measured with the same local corpus and toolchain.
- [ ] Results distinguish local measurements from external leaderboard figures.
- [ ] Both candidates remain available for the account integration comparison.
- [ ] A provisional candidate recommendation records gas, size headroom and known review limitations; final selection follows the project account measurements in PF-04 and correctness gate in PF-03.

issues.title: Add an isolated optimized SHAKE-256 hybrid verifier with the existing account ABI
issues.body:
## Outcome
Expose an optimized verifier class for new migrations and compatible already migrated accounts without changing keys or signature encoding. Directly deployed full accounts require separate lifecycle assessment in PF-06.

## Scope
- Preserve the actual derived storage addresses and Vec element layout, not only field spellings; test the baseline component layout against the optimized class in the migratable account context.
- Integrate the selected cumulative Falcon/NTT patch in an isolated, clearly versioned dependency variant, preserving a baseline for differential checks.
- Add a distinct optimized hybrid verifier class using the account's existing library-call interface.
- Preserve storage names/types read in the account's storage context: ecdsa_public_key and falcon_public_key.
- Preserve the public-key layout (29 felts), Falcon hint signature (60 felts), hybrid signature (62 felts), message encoding and NTT ordering.
- Keep ECDSA-first verification and require ECDSA AND Falcon over the same hash.
- For this verifier-only issue, preserve migration callbacks, registration hash, key derivation, backups and passkey behavior. PF-05 handles any separately justified replacement-tooling or account-API hardening.
- Account for shared-code effects on Poseidon and direct verifier variants.
- Prefer the compact candidate initially; compare full-wrapper sizes before accepting the current record.

Likely files: contracts/src/hybrid.cairo, contracts/src/lib.cairo, contracts/Scarb.toml, vendor/cairo-pq-verifiers/crates/falcon_512/src, vendor/cairo-pq-verifiers/crates/ntt/src and NOTICE.md.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Optimized class builds and exposes the current is_valid_signature ABI.
- [ ] Existing stored keys and browser signature fixtures verify through a library call.
- [ ] Invalid ECDSA or invalid Falcon independently causes rejection.
- [ ] Baseline remains available for comparison.
- [ ] Shared verifier variants pass regression checks.
- [ ] Dependencies and attribution are pinned; no automatic tracking of the live record.

issues.title: Establish differential correctness and review packed Falcon arithmetic
issues.body:
## Outcome
Demonstrate agreement with the intended Falcon-512 verification rules and identify security-sensitive assumptions introduced by optimization.

## Scope
- Compare optimized verifier, baseline and an independent Falcon reference on a reproducible public corpus. Treat the pinned Falcon specification/reference as the correctness authority, not the unaudited baseline; investigate baseline disagreements and document any intentional correction.
- Generate fresh keys/messages and signatures using the project's noble browser and Python paths; test each scheme with its matching hash-to-point signer. Cross-check SHAKE-compatible outputs without assuming Python v0 and noble v0.1 derive the same key from the same mnemonic.
- Test message/salt/key/signature/hint tampering, wrong lengths, noncanonical packing and salt bounds.
- Test the norm boundary and adjacent values, SHAKE rejection thresholds, byte order, block boundaries and unusual salts needing more than the common eight/nine blocks.
- Compare SHAKE bytes against independent SHAKE known-answer vectors and optimized hash-to-point coefficients against the reference. When optimized internal coefficients are unreduced, compare modulo q and also validate the exact bounds required by downstream arithmetic.
- Review bounded-int ranges, field wraparound assumptions, packed-lane interference, deferred NTT reductions, reciprocal reductions and packed norm extraction.
- Review specialized existing-keccak-syscall paths separately from future native-permutation proposals.
- Include available historical challenge breaks and persist new counterexamples locally; do not submit anything externally as part of this issue.
- Exercise expensive rejection paths and compare invalid-input cost to worst valid cost. The challenge's 1.25x rule is a useful regression target, not a proof of account safety.
- Review production compilation paths and feature attributes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Optimized verification agrees with the pinned specification/reference on the retained corpus; any baseline disagreement is understood, documented and tested.
- [ ] Browser and Python signatures verify against both implementations.
- [ ] Boundary and malformed-input regressions are committed.
- [ ] Every security-sensitive range/packing assumption has a readable explanation.
- [ ] Fuzzing seeds, coverage limits and unresolved findings are recorded.
- [ ] Challenge success is not described as an audit or proof of correctness.

## Sources
https://postquantum.provably.fast/reference/falcon512.py
https://postquantum.provably.fast/safe

issues.title: Benchmark hybrid transactions and enforce gas, class-size and libfunc limits
issues.body:
## Outcome
Choose a deployable candidate based on this project's actual accounts and demonstrate reproducible savings.

## Scope
- Recheck the selected candidate on the final guarded-replacement and account-upgrade paths after PF-05/PF-06; changing the thin account may change overhead or artifact sizes.
- Separate bare-verifier/no-syscall microbenchmarks from Starknet syscall-capable account tests; candidate paths using the existing keccak syscall must be measured in an appropriate Starknet environment.
- Measure baseline and candidates for bare Falcon verification, direct hybrid validation, migrated-account library-call validation, declare validation, direct full-account deploy validation and a complete transfer. The current thin migratable account has no __validate_deploy__; do not assume it supports the same deploy-account path.
- Measure complete migration transactions from representative newer and older wallet class versions, including the key-possession proof.
- Cover eight/nine-block signatures plus adverse valid and invalid cases.
- Track Sierra gas separately from VM resources, steps and actual receipt L1/L1-data/L2 resource usage.
- Measure the final hybrid class's CASM bytecode and serialized Sierra class size, not just the challenge account.
- Verify target-network allowed libfuncs rather than relying only on the current experimental list.
- Verify current target-network validation gas/step/class limits and record network/toolchain versions.
- Add reproducible CI gas/size regression budgets using public fixtures; document how deliberate baseline changes are approved.

Research-time challenge data: compact candidate 72,908 CASM felts versus current record 81,152, with a limit of 81,920. The compact candidate costs about 1.3% more gas but leaves more room for the hybrid wrapper. These figures must be rechecked on this project.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The selected optimized verifier and required account artifacts fit confirmed target-network limits. A non-selected candidate that exceeds limits is documented rather than blocking release of a valid candidate.
- [ ] Both candidate wrappers are compared, or an explicit reproducible build failure explains exclusion.
- [ ] Gas/step/size headroom and worst cases are documented.
- [ ] Measured full-transfer and migration savings replace speculative estimates.
- [ ] CI catches meaningful gas and size regressions.
- [ ] Monetary examples, if included, identify gas prices, STRK price and timestamp.

Likely files: .github/workflows/ci.yml, contracts/Scarb.toml, benchmark fixtures/harness and signer/mainnet_cost.mjs.

issues.title: Design and validate an atomic guarded verifier-replacement path
issues.body:
## Outcome
Reduce the risk of locking a migrated account by installing an incompatible verifier.

## Problem
set_verifier_class_hash currently checks self-authorization, registration and a nonzero class hash, but does not prove that the new verifier can validate the account's keys/signatures. Future transactions may become unusable after an incompatible change.

## Scope
- Explicitly document the raw setter and general upgrade entrypoint as remaining owner-authorized escape/bypass paths. If a new guarded entrypoint is additive, do not claim it enforces a global compatibility invariant across every owner-authorized upgrade.
- First evaluate a hybrid-signed atomic multicall using the existing setter followed by a helper that asserts candidate verification in the account's actual storage context. Merely calling is_valid_signature and ignoring a false return does not guard a switch. Introduce a new account entrypoint only if the existing API cannot support a robust solution; justify any required class upgrade.
- Keep the replacement transaction authorized by the existing ECDSA AND Falcon verifier.
- For SHAKE-to-SHAKE replacement, evaluate reading the replacement transaction hash/signature from get_tx_info in the assertion helper; the hash already commits to chain, account, nonce and candidate-call calldata. Do not embed that same transaction signature into its own signed calldata, which would create a circular signing dependency. If a separate compatibility proof is necessary, bind it to the operation, account, chain, candidate class hash and current keys/state; specify replay/domain separation. Scheme changes need a candidate-compatible proof.
- Preserve storage layout and existing key state. If an account API change is needed, document its upgrade transaction and compatibility with deployed thin account versions.
- Handle zero/undeclared class hashes, wrong ABI/return value, incompatible storage/layout, failing verification and syscall failure.
- Add wallet-kit construction/simulation and explicit version handling for accounts that only have the older setter.
- Treat candidate library code as trusted account-context code: it can access account storage and a malicious candidate may falsely accept or mutate state. Compatibility checks address accidental incompatibility, not hostile code. Use reviewed, pinned class hashes and verify expected storage remains unchanged apart from the verifier pointer.
- Treat reverting to the baseline as possible only while the active verifier still permits authorized transactions. Do not claim recovery from a verifier that rejects every transaction.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Incompatible candidate attempts through the guarded path revert the entire transaction, preserving the verifier pointer and all other storage. The documented raw setter is not covered by this guarantee.
- [ ] A compatible candidate can be installed and used for a subsequent hybrid transaction.
- [ ] ECDSA-only, Falcon-only and external-caller replacement attempts fail.
- [ ] Domain/replay and storage compatibility tests pass.
- [ ] Old-account upgrade requirements and tooling behavior are explicit.

Likely files: contracts/src/migratable.cairo, contracts/src/tests_migration.cairo and signer/pq_account_kit.mjs.

issues.title: Validate optimized-verifier migration and replacement across supported wallet accounts
issues.body:
## Outcome
Prove that the optimization works through real wallet migration and account-lifecycle paths.

## Scope
- Test fresh migrations using the optimized verifier for supported Argent/Ready callback versions, Xverse/OKX paths, Braavos and OpenZeppelin classes.
- Preserve atomic upgrade/migrate behavior, new-key possession proofs, protection-loss consent and storage collision checks.
- Test already migrated accounts switching from baseline SHAKE to optimized SHAKE, then making a transfer.
- Test Poseidon-to-SHAKE switching with explicit signer scheme changes only where the candidate signer supports the existing key. Python backup profile v0 and noble profile v0.1 can derive different Falcon keys from the same words; do not silently rederive or rotate a key. Document unsupported transitions and require a separately authorized key rotation if necessary.
- Test switching back to the known compatible baseline while the active verifier is functioning.
- Inventory older demo/deployed account ABIs; document or test any account-class upgrade required before guarded verifier replacement.
- Treat directly deployed HybridShakeAccount separately: it has no current verifier setter/upgrade path. Do not promise automatic in-place replacement.
- Verify ECDSA and Falcon key rotations and declare/signature-validation paths through the optimized verifier.
- Use disposable development/testnet keys and funds only. Public fixtures may use intentionally public keys; isolate any ephemeral secret test material from logs and committed artifacts.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Final candidate gas/step/size checks from PF-04 are repeated after any account or guarded-path changes; negative tests exercise actual transaction validation, not only direct dispatch with a spoofed caller.
- [ ] Supported wallet migration matrix has reproducible results and failed cases are explained.
- [ ] Address and stored keys are preserved; nonce and fee/balance changes match expected transaction behavior.
- [ ] Wrong-key possession proofs revert the entire migration.
- [ ] Subsequent hybrid transfer succeeds and ECDSA-only transfer is rejected.
- [ ] Existing safety checks remain enforced.
- [ ] Supported and unsupported existing-account upgrade routes are documented.

Likely files: contracts/src/tests_migration.cairo, contracts/src/tests_wallets.cairo, contracts/src/tests_browser.cairo, signer/wallet_migrate_demo.mjs and contracts/docs/wallet-coverage.md.

issues.title: Release a versioned optimized-verifier testnet integration and publish measured costs
issues.body:
## Outcome
Make the reviewed integration reproducible for wallet developers on testnet.

## Scope
- Publish exact source revisions, patch hashes, toolchain versions, artifact hashes and testnet verifier class hashes.
- Add explicit verifier-version selection to deployment/migration tooling; use pinned reviewed hashes.
- Update browser/setup/demo configuration without changing key derivation or backup profiles.
- Run end-to-end testnet browser signing, account migration, guarded verifier replacement and subsequent transfers.
- Record testnet transaction evidence and complete resource receipts.
- Document actual transfer/migration costs, one-time class declaration costs, limits, fallback prerequisites and unsupported account versions.
- Update NOTICE.md and README claims with attribution, round-three Falcon-512 terminology and experimental/testnet-only status.
- Prepare release artifacts and rollout commands first. Execute Sepolia or hosted-demo changes only within the user-authorized rollout scope; do not bundle an implicit mainnet deployment.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A developer can reproduce the documented testnet flow from a clean environment.
- [ ] The existing noble v0.1 browser backup fixtures restore the same keys and verify with optimized SHAKE. Python v0 fixtures retain their matching signer/backup behavior; no cross-profile key equivalence is assumed.
- [ ] Release metadata ties every deployed class to immutable source/artifacts.
- [ ] Cost claims use project measurements and clearly distinguish verification from full transaction cost.
- [ ] No real user keys or mainnet funds are used.
- [ ] Testnet-only status and outstanding review requirements remain visible.

Likely files: signer/browser_setup.mjs, signer/pq_account_kit.mjs, signer/mainnet_cost.mjs, docs/index.html, README.md and NOTICE.md.

issues.title: Prepare upstream adoption and independent security review for the optimized verifier
issues.body:
## Outcome
Create a reviewable path from challenge code to a production-quality dependency.

## Scope
- Prepare a minimal upstream patch/proposal with immutable provenance and contributor attribution.
- Explain the optimized algorithms and arithmetic invariants in readable form; retain or regenerate specialized code reproducibly where feasible.
- Provide independent-reference tests, malformed-input regressions, gas/size measurements and account integration evidence.
- Identify maintainability/toolchain risks from bounded-int internals and generated/minified implementation sections.
- Define an independent security review scope spanning verification, hybrid authorization, library-call storage, migration and verifier replacement.
- Track findings and require fixes/revalidation before any production recommendation.
- Deliver the upstream proposal and reviewer brief as drafts. External submissions or reviewer contact are separate from preparing this evidence bundle.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Actual independent review is explicitly distinguished from preparing its scope. If no review has been completed, production readiness remains open.
- [ ] Upstream submission draft and reproducible evidence bundle are ready.
- [ ] Review scope and unresolved findings are documented.
- [ ] Contributors and licenses are preserved.
- [ ] Production readiness requires independent review and resolution of relevant findings.
- [ ] Challenge acceptance is not presented as OpenZeppelin endorsement.

## Source
https://postquantum.provably.fast/safe

issues.title: Track native Keccak permutation support as a future Falcon optimization
issues.body:
## Outcome
Keep a concrete future optimization path without making the current integration depend on a protocol change.

## Scope
- Track SNIP-32/raw Keccak-f[1600] support and related prover research against primary sources.
- Distinguish Cairo optimizations and specialized use of today's keccak syscall from a new raw permutation syscall.
- When a usable implementation exists, estimate and then measure savings with the same public Falcon corpus.
- Check SHAKE padding, rate/capacity, repeated squeezing, libfunc availability and validation restrictions.
- Retain a software implementation for compatibility and reference comparisons.
- Record an explicit adoption trigger: target-network availability plus differential correctness, limits and account-level savings.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Current protocol status, primary sources and adoption prerequisites are recorded.
- [ ] No present-day savings claim assumes an unavailable syscall.
- [ ] A future experiment has defined correctness and full-account performance criteria.

## Sources
https://community.starknet.io/t/snip-32-expose-keccak-f-1600-permutation-syscall/115770
https://postquantum.provably.fast/agent-brief.md

Deferred research; does not block PF-07.

issues.title: Document Falcon-512 scheme versioning and assess eventual FN-DSA migration
issues.body:
## Outcome
Avoid conflating current round-three Falcon support with eventual FN-DSA/FIPS 206 compatibility.

## Scope
- Check current NIST primary sources when working this issue.
- Correct scheme descriptions that imply the current implementation already conforms to finalized FN-DSA.
- Record current signing/message/encoding parameters and pinned key-derivation/signer versions.
- Assess eventual differences in key generation, signatures, domain separation and message preprocessing once specifications are available.
- Define explicit signer/verifier scheme version metadata and a future migration approach.
- Do not alter existing mnemonic-to-key derivation or claim key/signature compatibility without evidence.
- Keep any future scheme transition separate from the current ABI-preserving gas optimization.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Current Falcon support and standardization status are accurately documented.
- [ ] Scheme/signer/verifier versions can be identified without relying on a live leaderboard.
- [ ] Compatibility questions and future migration triggers are recorded.
- [ ] Current recovery reproducibility is preserved.

Deferred research; does not block PF-07. Any essential terminology corrections can ship with PF-07.
